targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-485g (first non-vacuous trained-OFC-head behavioural test): readiness MET (cross-candidate bias range 0.171 >= 0.05 floor, 2/3 seeds; head weight-delta 6.32, genuinely trained), C3 frozen-head silence control PASS, but C1 devaluation shift {0.001,0.0,0.010} << 0.05 (0/3) and C2 between-context TV ~0 (degenerate) -- a genuine 0.17 bias RANGE with ZERO behavioural conversion. Adjudicated substrate_ceiling / non_contributory, NOT a weakens: the OFC mechanism is a faithful translation (lit_conf 0.863) and was not given a fair conversion test (the outcome-coupled driver supplies zero anti-range gradient at low threat -- the suppression C1 measures -- and the devalued-state bias range, the decisive conversion-vs-conditioning disambiguator, was not recorded). The manifest's MECH-439 F-dominance self-route is an analogy to the broader conversion-ceiling pattern, NOT a mechanism measurable in 485g's isolated-OFC-softmax loop (F is absent from this readout). Routed to V3-EXQ-485h (disambiguating redesign: record devalued-state bias range + per-task-role-context range, close the driver gap with a paired high-threat/devalued contrast, optional live-E3-selector arm to test F-dominance directly). SD-033b + MECH-263 stay candidate / pending_retest_after_substrate -- sole genuine experimental entry for both; do not let this define exp_conf.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: The implemented SD-033b trained state_bias_head produced a genuine non-vacuous cross-candidate bias range (0.171 >= 0.05 floor) for the first time (V3-EXQ-485g) but ZERO behavioural conversion (C1 devaluation shift <<0.05, C2 between-context TV ~0). The substrate-readout starvation of 485e/485f is fixed; the residual gap is CONVERSION (threat-conditioning of the bias and/or bias->selection conversion). The 485h redesign records the devalued-state bias range (the conversion-vs-conditioning disambiguator) + closes the driver's missing low-threat anti-range gradient. Do NOT mint a MECH-439 substrate entry from this run -- the conversion-ceiling cluster owns that and 485g cannot measure F in its isolated-softmax loop.

failure_record_entry.metric: C1 devaluation_selection_shift {0.001,0.0,0.010} << 0.05 margin (0/3) AND C2 between_context_selection_tv ~0 (degenerate, 0/3), with readiness MET (bias range 0.171 >= 0.05, head delta 6.32) and C3 control PASS -- genuine 0.17 bias range, zero behavioural conversion

learning_extracted: First non-vacuous 485 result -- the 485e (range-starved) -> 485f (vacuous-readiness) -> 485g lineage is a sequence of test-instrumentation fixes; 485g is the first run where readiness is genuinely met (0.17 range) and the claim still does not convert. The wall moved from substrate-readout starvation to conversion.

The manifest's MECH-439 F-dominance self-route over-reads its own loop: the DV is the isolated OFC softmax with modulatory selection authority OFF, so F is not in this loop. F-dominance remains a credible broader-pattern hypothesis to test by routing the OFC bias through the live E3 selector (485h optional arm), not a mechanism measured here.

The outcome-coupled driver (adv_k = gain*threat*(mean_harm - harm_k)) is zero at threat~0, so the head gets no signal to flatten range when devalued -- exactly the suppression C1 measures. C1 was hard by construction; the non-circular fix is an explicit paired high-threat/devalued contrast term.

The decisive disambiguator -- OFC bias range at the devalued state (and per task-role context) -- was not recorded, so T (threat-conditioning gap) and F (conversion ceiling) are indistinguishable on this run. 485h is designed to record it.

cluster_pattern.shape: negative-control-passes + readiness-passes (non-vacuous) + every discrimination criterion fails -- the substrate-ceiling fingerprint, here at the OFC-bias->behaviour conversion link
